subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview accept any parser-verified JavaScript/TypeScript identifier or member expression as a source reference, or keep a deliberately narrow root allowlist and add only demonstrated safe roots?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the boundary between safe source references and potentially sensitive review-bundle content, which needs maintainer ownership beyond a mechanical regex adjustment.

options.title: Adopt parser-verified references
options.body: Accept syntactically verified JavaScript/TypeScript identifier and member-expression values, with regressions proving literals and non-source inputs remain blocked.

options.title: Extend approved roots only
options.body: Retain the narrow allowlist and add only specific roots such as `ctx` or `environment` when their safety contract is documented and tested.

options.title: Add an explicit override
options.body: Keep the current default boundary and provide a narrowly scoped, documented override for exceptional review bundles.

recommendation.title: Adopt parser-verified references
recommendation.body: Accept syntactically verified JavaScript/TypeScript identifier and member-expression values, with regressions proving literals and non-source inputs remain blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current parser-backed boundary and is the clearest history-based routing candidate.
